1. Purpose
This matrix sets who may approve a purchase request or purchase order, and up to what value. It is the
matrix referred to in Purchase Policy §5.2.
2. How limits are measured
2.1 Every limit is a limit on the gross value including VAT of one document. Freight and packing
charged on the order count towards the gross value.
2.2 A limit is per document, not per day or per supplier.
2.3 Splitting one requirement into several orders to stay inside a limit is not allowed. Orders for the
same item from the same supplier raised within seven days of each other are treated as one
requirement.
3. The limits
3.1 Each role's approval limit, gross including VAT:

£500,000

£5,000,000

3.2 A document within the raiser's own limit is approved when it is submitted. Ledgerline records the
raiser as the approver.
3.3 A document above the raiser's limit goes to the raiser's manager. If the manager's limit does not
cover it, it goes on up the line to the first person whose limit does.
3.4 Above £5,000,000 the order needs the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline.

then records the MD's approval.

4. Who may not approve
4.1 Nobody may approve a document they raised (Purchase Policy §5.3). Ledgerline refuses with
ERR-APR-0003.
4.2 Integration and service accounts (role SYS-ADMIN, for example SVC_AGENT) have no approval
authority under this matrix, whatever their technical permissions in Ledgerline. A document approved
by a service account is treated as unapproved and must be cancelled or re-approved by a person.
4.3 An approver on leave may delegate in writing to someone of the same or a higher role for a stated
period. Delegation to a lower role is not allowed.
5. Examples
5.1 Emma Clarke (purchase executive) raises an order for 2,000 battery packs at £119.00: basic
£238,000, VAT 20% £47,600, gross £285,600. The gross is above her £250,000 limit, so the order goes
to her manager, Daniel Okafor (purchase manager, limit £1,000,000), for approval.
5.2 The same order at basic value alone (£238,000) would look within her limit. That is why limits are
measured on the gross value (§2.1).
5.3 An order of £720,000 gross raised by the senior buyer goes to the purchase manager. An order of
£1,200,000 gross raised by anyone in purchasing goes to the plant head, Henrik Weber.
6. Review
6.1 The plant head reviews this matrix every April, and when the organisation changes.

1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every
pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit
(NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost
centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is
£50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry
new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent
to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask
Finance.

5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit
must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's
limit covers the order's gross value.
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for
reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the
remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country
is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released
before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is
Released.

Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy
When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?
Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request
in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order
without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.
Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?
Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed
cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre
cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost
centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an
order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.
No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity
requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you
must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.
How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?
Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order,
including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax
has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix,
section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is
sufficient to cover that gross amount.
Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?
No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls
well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out
the approval.
Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already
signed off?
Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from
it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order.
If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval
must be obtained.
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process

set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.
What rate should I enter on the purchase order?
Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy
prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If
market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section
7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.
Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?
Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any
supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax
codes ending in -RC.
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.

1. Purpose
1. Purpose
This procedure sets out the required method for booking inbound deliveries into Ledgerline ERP across both the Manchester plant and the Leeds unit. The objective is to maintain an accurate record of physical stock, ensure raw materials and components are made available for the production lines without delay, and provide purchasing with clear confirmation that ordered goods have arrived in sound condition.
Operational Context
In daily practice, every delivery arriving at the loading bay must be checked against the physical delivery note and entered into Ledgerline ERP before items are moved to their designated storage bins. Once entered, the system updates inventory balances, clears outstanding commitments on the relevant purchase order, and creates the accrual required by the accounts department to match the supplier invoice. A signed copy of the delivery documentation must be filed at the receiving site.
Common Errors
Staff frequently make mistakes when dealing with partial shipments or busy delivery periods. Common issues include:
Moving deliveries straight to the assembly benches or stores racking before booking them onto the system.
Accepting damaged cartons without endorsing the carrier delivery sheet or notifying purchasing.
Booking the full purchase order quantity when only a partial delivery has been unloaded.
Failing to verify delivery notes against the original order details, leading to the receipt of incorrect part specifications.
Practical Guidance
Receiving staff should always complete a thorough outer carton check before signing the carrier handheld terminal. If the delivery note is missing or illegible, keep the consignment in the quarantine bay until purchasing can supply the correct purchase order paperwork. When booking receipts, enter only the physical count actually verified on the pallet, rather than the quantity printed on the packing slip. Always complete the transaction before the end of the working shift so that stock levels remain true for assembly planning.
2. Scope
2. Scope
Purpose and Coverage
This procedure covers the physical intake, checking, and system booking of all incoming consignments across both the Manchester plant and the Leeds unit. It applies to production parts, raw materials, tooling, and consumable supplies delivered against existing purchase orders. Items arriving without purchase orders, customer returns, and inter-site transfers fall outside this specific process and follow separate procedures.
Operational Practice
Once signed for, the shipment is entered on the terminal so that stock levels update immediately and the inventory becomes available for production.
Common Errors and Practical Guidance
Staff sometimes sign carrier sheets before checking carton integrity, preventing later claims for damaged contents.
Inward items are occasionally moved to the assembly floor prior to booking onto the system, which causes stock discrepancies.
Always check that supplier delivery notes match the purchase order lines line by line.
When an over-delivery or damaged item arrives, hold the goods in the bay and inform purchasing promptly.
3. Responsibilities
3. Responsibilities
Purpose and Scope
This section sets out the distribution of duties between the goods inwards team, the quality inspection staff, purchasing, and finance. Clear responsibility prevents discrepancies between physical stock and the inventory ledger, whilst ensuring suppliers are only paid for items received in good order.
Operational Practice
Quality control inspectors examine specified items, such as drive assemblies and frames, updating the inspection status in the system before items are released to the warehouse racks.
Purchasing staff resolve discrepancies where delivered quantities or descriptions differ from the original purchase order, liaising directly with the vendor.
Accounts payable match the recorded receipt against the supplier invoice to allow payment.
Common Errors
This creates phantom shortages on screen, causing purchasing to chase parts that are already in the building. Another regular failure occurs when warehouse staff assume the quantities printed on the supplier advice note are correct without a manual tally, leading to immediate stock record inaccuracies. Furthermore, uninspected goods are sometimes moved into general stock because personnel overlook the quarantine stage.
Practical Guidance
Always complete the system entry before moving pallets out of the unloading bay.
Mark damaged packaging immediately on the delivery sheet before signing for the carrier.
Keep quarantined items physically separated in the designated holding area until inspection signs them off.
If paperwork is missing, seek immediate guidance from purchasing rather than setting the delivery aside without a record.
4. Abbreviations
5. Procedure
5.1 Check the supplier's delivery note against the purchase order number. Only released orders (RL) can be received; Ledgerline refuses others with ERR-GRN-0102.
5.2 On INV-GRN-03, type the PO number and press Fetch. Count the goods, enter the quantity received and the supplier's delivery note number in Remarks, and press Save.
5.3 A part delivery gets its own GRN. You cannot receive more than the order's balance (ERR-GRN-0204).
5.4 Lithium-cell parts are received into the quality hold warehouse WH-MAN-QC and stay there until Quality releases them to the fire-cell area of Manchester main stores.
5.5 Damaged packaging on a battery delivery: refuse the parcel, photograph it and tell Quality (SOP-QUA-002).
5. Procedure: notes and common mistakes
Common mistakes
Attempting to receive an order before purchasing has released it. Warehouse staff often take delivery paperwork straight to the terminal and key the reference while the order is still held in an earlier state. When this happens, do not put the paperwork aside or guess the status; the buyer must release the order before goods receipt can proceed.
Boo

5.1 Check the supplier's delivery note against the purchase order number. Only released orders (RL) can be received; Ledgerline refuses others with ERR-GRN-0102.
5.2 On INV-GRN-03, type the PO number and press Fetch. Count the goods, enter the quantity received and the supplier's delivery note number in Remarks, and press Save.
5.3 A part delivery gets its own GRN. You cannot receive more than the order's balance (ERR-GRN-0204).
5.4 Lithium-cell parts are received into the quality hold warehouse WH-MAN-QC and stay there until Quality releases them to the fire-cell area of Manchester main stores.
5.5 Damaged packaging on a battery delivery: refuse the parcel, photograph it and tell Quality (SOP-QUA-002).

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 5. Procedure › 5. Procedure: notes and common mistakes › Common mistakes
units.text:
Common mistakes
Attempting to receive an order before purchasing has released it. Warehouse staff often take delivery paperwork straight to the terminal and key the reference while the order is still held in an earlier state. When this happens, do not put the paperwork aside or guess the status; the buyer must release the order before goods receipt can proceed.
Booking lithium-cell deliveries into general stock. Battery items and cells must never be posted into the general picking bays. The destination location on screen must show WH-MAN-QC. Bypassing this step leaves hazardous stock outside the containment area and prevents Quality from tracking the consignment.
Forgetting to enter the delivery note reference in Remarks. Stores staff sometimes key the counts, hit Save, and omit the supplier's paperwork reference. Accounts cannot match the supplier invoice without this cross-reference, which creates queries during invoice clearance.
Attempting to over-receive a line against the purchase order balance. If the supplier sends more items than the outstanding balance, the system halts the transaction with ERR-GRN-0204. Do not increase the order balance yourself; the excess items must be dealt with according to the purchasing instructions.
Processing a split delivery on an old goods receipt record. Each physical consignment requires its own distinct transaction. Staff must not overwrite earlier receipts when booking in partial shipments.

loc.section: What to check on the screen

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 5. Procedure › 5. Procedure: notes and common mistakes › What to check on the screen
units.text:
What to check on the screen
The document status field following the fetch operation. Confirm that the status reads RL. If any other status code displays, the transaction cannot be saved.
The item description and unit of measure displayed on INV-GRN-03. A mismatch between individual units and boxed sets is a frequent source of discrepancies.
The open balance figure on the line items. Check this quantity against the physical delivery note before typing the count. This confirms that previous split shipments have been recorded accurately and shows the remaining amount permitted on the order.
The warehouse code populated for sensitive stock. Verify that all lithium-cell components show WH-MAN-QC as the receiving warehouse before committing the record to the system.
The text string entered into Remarks. Check that the supplier's paperwork reference is typed without errors or missing characters before pressing Save.

loc.section: What to do when something does not look right

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 5. Procedure › 5. Procedure: notes and common mistakes › What to do when something does not look right
units.text:
What to do when something does not look right
When the system displays ERR-GRN-0102, contact the purchasing team to confirm the order status. Do not attempt to force the receipt or alter the reference on the screen.
When an over-delivery triggers ERR-GRN-0204, halt the transaction. Receive only the valid balance if instructed, or hold the entire delivery in the receiving bay while contacting purchasing. Never adjust system figures to absorb extra stock.
When battery cartons or lithium-cell outer packaging show tears, dents, dampness, or crushed corners, refuse the parcel from the carrier immediately. Do not bring the items into the building. Take clear photographs of the damage while the carrier is present and alert Quality in accordance with SOP-QUA-002.
If physical counts differ from the supplier's delivery note, record only the count verified on the floor. Note any shortages on the carrier's paperwork and adjust the entered quantity to match the physical count before saving.

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 6. Records › 6. Records › Purpose of Goods Receipt Records
units.text:
Purpose of Goods Receipt Records
Goods receipt records provide verifiable proof that materials, assemblies, and consumables delivered to the Manchester works or Leeds unit match purchase orders and delivery notes. These records establish stock ownership, update inventory balances, and allow accounts payable to match purchase invoices against confirmed receipts. Without completed records, stock remains unrecorded on the shop floor, creating discrepancies between physical holdings and the system.

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 6. Records › 6. Records › Routine Recording Practice
units.text:
Routine Recording Practice
When a delivery arrives, goods inwards staff check the consignment against the carrier documentation and Northbridge purchase order. Staff enter the details into Ledgerline ERP to record the receipt, generate the internal receipt transaction, and print the goods received paperwork. Physical delivery notes, advice notes, and carrier consignment sheets are stamped, annotated with the system reference, and filed in goods inwards. Once stock is inspected, staff transfer accepted items to stores bins and record any quarantine movement directly in the system.

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 6. Records › 6. Records › Common Errors and Omissions
units.text:
Common Errors and Omissions
Staff frequently fail to record deliveries immediately upon arrival, allowing unchecked boxes to sit in bays while production staff remove parts unrecorded. Another regular issue is accepting deliveries without retaining the carrier proof of delivery, which leaves Northbridge unable to contest short deliveries or transit damage. Staff also misplace delivery notes prior to filing, or enter receipts against incorrect order lines when suppliers deliver partial quantities.

units.heading: Goods Receipt › 6. Records › 6. Records › Practical Tips
units.text:
Practical Tips
Always compare the delivery note line by line with the purchase order before entering data into Ledgerline ERP.
Stamp and initial every paper delivery note the moment packages are counted off the vehicle.
Never permit production staff to take parts from the goods inwards area until the receipt entry is fully posted.
Keep the goods inwards filing trays sorted by supplier name to avoid paper backlogs at month end.

Purpose and Ledgerline practice
This restriction maintains basic financial control across Manchester and Leeds. In Ledgerline ERP, the user account that creates a purchase requisition or purchase order is logged against the record. Even if an employee holds delegated authority for the spend category, the software will not permit self-authorisation, and bypassing this via shared logins is strictly prohibited. An independent set of eyes must verify the business need and budget availability before the order proceeds to the supplier.
Common errors
Staff frequently attempt to approve requisitions they entered on behalf of an absent colleague. Ledgerline records the person who typed the entry, not the person who requested the goods. Another common issue arises when managers alter lines on a junior colleague's draft order; altering the document often reassigns ownership to the manager, leaving them unable to sign it off.
Practical tips
Ask the person who actually requires the items to enter the requisition directly.
If you must raise an order for your department, send it to your own line manager or designated peer for approval.
Check the creator field in Ledgerline before starting the authorisation routine to avoid system rejections.

Approval limits (2016)

All purchase orders, stock requisitions, and capital commitments raised across the Manchester factory and the Leeds unit must comply with the company authorisation tiers. Staff are reminded that all limits apply strictly to the net value before VAT. Value added tax must not be included when determining which band of authority an order falls under, but the tax portion must still be entered correctly for accounting purposes.

Orders must not be artificially split into multiple smaller orders to circumvent approval thresholds. System audits run regularly from the finance office, and any attempt to bypass controls by raising parallel requisitions against the same supplier account will be flagged. Where an ongoing service or regular intake of cycle components requires multiple deliveries, the total anticipated commitment over the entire order period governs the level of authorisation needed.

Department managers hold delegated authority up to their established tier for operational overheads and regular production inventory. Requisitions that exceed standard department limits require counter-signing by a director. Any non-budgeted capital expenditure, building works, or tooling investments require the formal endorsement of the managing director before commitments are placed with suppliers.

When processing through Ledgerline ERP, users must select the designated authoriser from the standard workflow list. An order remains at an unapproved status and cannot be printed, transmitted, or converted into an active commitment until the approving manager enters their sign-off. If an authoriser is absent from the business, their designated deputy may act only where formal standing arrangements exist within the system administration settings. Emergency verbal approvals are not recognised by the accounts department, and invoices received without a corresponding approved order will be held in query pending retrospective review.

1. Scope
Purpose and Application
This section defines the reach of the policy across Northbridge Cycles, governing every claim for
travel, accommodation, and incidental expenses. It applies to all permanent staff, temporary workers,
and contractors operating from the Manchester factory, the Leeds unit, or on business elsewhere in the
country.
Practical Operation
Expenditure must arise wholly and necessarily from company duties, such as visiting an independent
bike shop, attending technical trials, or travelling between sites. Staff must secure approval from their
department head before arranging journeys. Once travel is complete, claimants enter the details into the
finance ledger module, attaching itemised receipts for verification by the accounts office.
Common Errors
• Assuming routine travel between home and the usual place of work is claimable.
• Booking regional travel without obtaining prior line management authorisation.
• Submitting credit card slips rather than detailed VAT receipts.
Practical Tips
• Verify that expenditure falls squarely within company business before paying out of pocket.
• Seek written approval well in advance of making major bookings.
• Retain paper receipts immediately to prevent delays during ledger reconciliation.

This section sets out the arrangements for booking passenger transport when travelling on company

Bookings must be arranged through the accounts office rather than settled on personal payment cards,

The most frequent issue is purchasing fully flexible tickets without prior agreement from the
department manager. Staff also frequently err by upgrading class of travel at their own discretion on
journeys that fall short of the qualifying thresholds, or by adding seat reservations and supplementary
charges that have not been sanctioned. The finance team will not reimburse unapproved upgrades.

Purpose and Operation
The claims procedure exists to reimburse staff for legitimate expenditure incurred while undertaking
company business on behalf of the Manchester factory or the Leeds unit. Expenditure must be wholly
necessary, and staff should neither gain nor lose financially as a result of their duties.
In practice, claimants log into the legacy system and access screen AP-EXP-09 to generate an expense
header. Each line item is entered individually, detailing the business purpose, the cost centre, and the
ledger allocation. Once the claim is compiled, all supporting physical documentation must be collated.
Receipts are physically grouped, referenced to the system line items, and passed alongside the
electronic batch to the claimant's line manager for review. The line manager checks the business
justification and verifies that all items match before posting the approval in the system. Once approved,
the claim passes automatically to the purchase ledger clerk for payment processing.
Common Errors
Claimants also regularly omit receipts for individual lines over ten pounds, or provide unitemised debit
slips rather than detailed VAT receipts. Other recurrent issues include entering incorrect cost centre
strings on screen AP-EXP-09, conflating mileage and public transport costs into a single line, and
submitting claims before securing prior verbal approval for travel from the department head.
Practical Tips
• Retain paper receipts at the point of sale and place them in an envelope kept specifically for the trip.
• Input expenses into screen AP-EXP-09 incrementally throughout the month rather than waiting until
the end of the allowable window.
• Check that the total figure on screen AP-EXP-09 matches the paper total exactly before sending the
notification to the line manager.

units.text:
Purpose and scope
This section sets out the arrangements for booking passenger transport when travelling on company
business between the Manchester works, the Leeds unit, and external locations. The objective is to
control expenditure while ensuring staff arrive safely and in good time for their duties.

Working practice
Bookings must be arranged through the accounts office rather than settled on personal payment cards,
using the designated travel account. Staff should request tickets as soon as the travel dates are settled,
selecting fixed services rather than open tickets wherever the schedule permits. Tickets for inter-site
journeys between Manchester and Leeds must always be standard class.

The most frequent issue is purchasing fully flexible tickets without prior agreement from the
department manager. Staff also frequently err by upgrading class of travel at their own discretion on
journeys that fall short of the qualifying thresholds, or by adding seat reservations and supplementary
charges that have not been sanctioned. The finance team will not reimburse unapproved upgrades.

units.heading: Travel and Expenses Policy › 5. Claims › 5. Claims › Purpose and Operation
units.text:
Purpose and Operation
The claims procedure exists to reimburse staff for legitimate expenditure incurred while undertaking
company business on behalf of the Manchester factory or the Leeds unit. Expenditure must be wholly
necessary, and staff should neither gain nor lose financially as a result of their duties.
In practice, claimants log into the legacy system and access screen AP-EXP-09 to generate an expense
header. Each line item is entered individually, detailing the business purpose, the cost centre, and the
ledger allocation. Once the claim is compiled, all supporting physical documentation must be collated.
Receipts are physically grouped, referenced to the system line items, and passed alongside the
electronic batch to the claimant's line manager for review. The line manager checks the business
justification and verifies that all items match before posting the approval in the system. Once approved,
the claim passes automatically to the purchase ledger clerk for payment processing.

units.heading: Travel and Expenses Policy › 5. Claims › 5. Claims › Common Errors
units.text:
Common Errors
Claimants also regularly omit receipts for individual lines over ten pounds, or provide unitemised debit
slips rather than detailed VAT receipts. Other recurrent issues include entering incorrect cost centre
strings on screen AP-EXP-09, conflating mileage and public transport costs into a single line, and
submitting claims before securing prior verbal approval for travel from the department head.

units.heading: Travel and Expenses Policy › 5. Claims › 5. Claims › Practical Tips
units.text:
Practical Tips
• Retain paper receipts at the point of sale and place them in an envelope kept specifically for the trip.
• Input expenses into screen AP-EXP-09 incrementally throughout the month rather than waiting until
the end of the allowable window.
• Check that the total figure on screen AP-EXP-09 matches the paper total exactly before sending the
notification to the line manager.

Purpose and scope
This section sets out the arrangements for accommodation and subsistence when staff travel on
company business. The objective is to ensure that employees stay in reasonable, clean, and secure
accommodation without the business incurring unnecessary cost, while keeping expense processing
consistent between Manchester and Leeds.

All accommodation bookings should be arranged in advance wherever practicable. The nightly ceilings
of £150 outside London and £210 in London include breakfast and any local taxes. If a booking cannot
be secured within these ceilings, staff must obtain written approval from their department head before
confirming the room.

incurred, and itemised receipts are required for every purchase.

breaching the room limit.

personal responsibility of the employee.

final claim.

Purchase Policy
Version history
1. Purpose
This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.
2. Scope
It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.
3. Requests before orders
3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost centre that will carry the spend.
3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less.
3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.
4. Cost centres and budgets
4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent to the supplier.
4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask Finance.
5. Approval limits
5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's limit covers the order's gross value.
6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors and any other item marked lithium-cell in the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed with them.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 5% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the remarks.
8. Tax
8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).
9. Records
9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released before the supplier is told to deliver.
9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is Released.
